newsitem.title: ALBANIA: First foreign troops start Albania withdrawal.
newsitem.headline: First foreign troops start Albania withdrawal.

text.p: The Italian-led multinational protection force in Albania on Wednesday began its gradual withdrawal as Romanian troops left the southern town of Gjirokaster for Durres port.

Force spokesman Lieutenant Colonel Giovanni Bernardi said the 390 Romanians would leave Durres by ship on Friday. The same day, Italians of the 151st infantry regiment would leave the southern town of Kucove and return home by ship from Vlore.

Some 7,000 troops from 11 nations were deployed across Albania in April in Operation Alba (Italian for dawn) after a violent uprising sparked by the collapse of get-rich-quick savings funds left the army and police in disarray and state authority in tatters.
Their mandate was to protect aid deliveries and ensure elections on June 29 and subsequent run-offs ran smoothly. The withdrawal is due to be completed by August 12.

A senior politician of the leftist coalition which will form the next government after a landslide election victory has told diplomats he would have liked the force to stay until the end of the year to give the new government time to reorganise the national army and police.

Former Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky, head of an Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe mission which oversaw the election, said last week an international working group would be set up to help restore law and order and start economic reconstruction.

One person has been killed in an incident with the multinational force, an Albanian who shot at a guard in the central town of Elbasan last month after trying to sell him drugs. The guard returned fire, hitting the man who later died in hospital.
A handful of soldiers have been injured in the four months, none of them in conflicts. Most were hit by falling bullets.
